annotations.text:
SHIPPED

The phone does not say the place at all. Sorted by place the drawer label says the room once for a whole run; sorted A–Z the room is not the question you are asking, and the switch is one tap.

Beyond the ranking going away: the tile is the same height in both orderings, so the grid stops going ragged when you switch the sort, and the second line can never compete with anything.

Desktop is unchanged — it has a column for the place, and a column is not prose.

BEFORE

The species and the place drawn as one prose block under the name, ranked apart by a size and a shade.

That is the treatment for two facts of one kind. These are two kinds: the species is what the plant IS, the place is where it happens to be standing. Ranking them only made the eye read both lines to find out which was which — and on a narrow phone the loser truncated mid-word.

The three that were not taken. All of them answer 'different kind of fact' by giving the place a different FORM; the shipped answer gives it no form at all, which turned out to be the one that also fixes the ragged grid and the truncation.

LABEL REGISTER

The place set in the app's own place type — the specimen the drawer label uses to say SLAAPKAMER above a group. The register change does the separating: no dot, no contest between greys.

Why not: still a second line to read, and caps run long.

ITS OWN LANE

A chip on the picture, a fixed 84px lane on the row. Also gives a constant tile height.

Why not: a chip on a photograph is busier than one on paper, and the lane costs every row 84px for a fact you only sometimes want.

WITH ITS PIN

The place keeps its prose and gains the glyph the form puts over 'Where it lives'.

Why not: one pin per row and per tile is a lot of small marks on a page whose whole manner is quiet, and 11px of pin is close to mush.
